# Tina - the musical

![Tina turner the musical poster](Tina-the-musical.jpg)

Gait and I went to see the Tina Turner musical last night at the Bristol Hippodrome. As a man of a certain age, and because I was driving, I thought that having a drink before watching a 3 hour show might be a bad idea. We opted instead for some bottles of water and some pick and mix. Going in hard. 

It was the right choice because I am also a man of a certain height and the Hippodrome, while historic and iconic, was designed in an age when rickets and malnutrition limited both height and lifespans. It was a tight fit for me and I leaned into my wife rather than the elderly lady next to me who looked rather uncomfortable herself. Thankfully, because I watch movies, I know plenty about CIA torture survival and mental coping mechanisms. I munched my way through the pick and mix and focussed on the show. 

The show itself is incredible. A lot of wife beating, hardship and kids being whipped with belts which was rough in the first half. It helps to know in the end that Tina gets to do the soundtrack for both GoldenEye (song not featured in musical) and Mad Max: Thunderdome (in the musical). 

The cast are spectacular and I was blown away by the lead playing Tina, Elle Ma-Kinga N'Zuzi. Elle must have incredible cardio as it was 3 hours of her dancing and singing. Her training regime must be intense enough that even the most hardened Royal Marine would ask her to 'ease up a bit'. The finale being a particular highlight where a series of hits were belted out. They did a great job of tying in the music with the events in her life.
